evidence: Capacitance-voltage (C-V) measurements and leakage current density–voltage (J-V) measurements were performed using an HP 4194 impedance analyzer and HP 4140B picoammeter/dc voltage source, respectively. The CET was calculated from the accumulation capacitance. The chemical bonding status and the changes in the quantitative composition of the dielectric thin films were studied by XPS using Mg Kα as x-ray source. XPS peak deconvolution was attempted using a Gaussian-Lorentzian line shape after background subtraction. Figure 1 shows the variations in the CET of the HfO2 films grown on (a) thick and (b) thin SiO2 layers as a function of the PDA temperature ranging from 760 to 1000 °C. Figure 1(c) shows the cross-section transmission electron microscopy image of the 1.4-nm-thick SiO2 film.
